Marissa / team,

Thanks for the ping — dug into the March 1 incident. Summary (high level):
- Root cause: transient KV-cache eviction combined with an autoscaler throttle during a sudden traffic burst to model A. That caused request queuing and a handful of 5xx retries.
- Impact window: ~06:18:12 - 06:24:40 UTC (6m28s) affecting 0.6% of requests at peak

Short-term mitigations we can offer immediately:
- Route FinServe traffic to a warmed instance pool (reserved burst capacity) during peak hours
- Enable prefix KV caching retention for their prefix set to reduce cache churn
- Fallback routing to a compatible model variant with lower latency for tail requests

Longer-term / premium option: Dedicated pool (premium-tier) with commitment: 99.95% uptime SLA and target p95 latency <= 200-250ms for their primary region (US-West). This includes priority autoscale and a reserved buffer of GPUs during their peak windows. Wed also provide an incident report packet (attached).

Id propose: 30-day premium pilot (no extra charge) so the customer can validate latency and we can tune policies. If they accept, we prepare an addendum that defines the SLA and credit formula.

Attachment: se-incident-summary-march1.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

Happy to join a call with FinServe and walk through the technical controls.

— Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
